study_name: Meno-J Theory Study 3: Historical J-Jump Casebook 2
case: Miasma, sanitation, transmission, and germ theories

method.qualification: This is a historical-philosophical calibration, not medical guidance or proof that one timeless germ theory replaced one timeless miasma theory.

sources.title: On the Mode of Communication of Cholera, second edition
supports: Snow argued for a disease-specific waterborne route using outbreak comparisons, exceptions, and water-supply evidence rather than a cultured organism.

sources.title: On the Mode of Communication of Cholera
supports: The enlarged edition included household deaths and water-supply evidence, not only the famous map.

sources.title: Die Aetiologie, der Begriff und die Prophylaxis des Kindbettfiebers
supports: Semmelweis presented mortality tables, cadaveric and other decaying material, chlorine washing, and competing etiological claims.

sources.title: On the Organized Corpuscles Existing in the Atmosphere
supports: Pasteur framed spontaneous generation as an experimental question and argued that apparent generation resulted from unnoticed contamination or experimental error.

sources.authors: Louis Pasteur; Smithsonian Libraries and Archives
sources.title: Memoir on Lactic Fermentation
supports: Pasteur connected a specific fermentation process with living microorganisms, contributing a laboratory ontology broader than a single epidemic route.

sources.title: The Etiology of Anthrax Based on the Developmental History of Bacillus anthracis
supports: Koch linked a particular organism and life cycle to anthrax using microscopy, cultivation, and transmission experiments.

sources.title: The Etiology of Tuberculosis
supports: Koch used staining, repeated detection, culture, and inoculation to argue for a specific infectious cause of tuberculosis.

sources.title: The Aetiology of Tuberculosis, English excerpts
supports: Koch treated tuberculosis as a specific infectious disease and connected etiology with possible prevention.

sources.title: Mythological Endings: John Snow and the History of American Epidemiology
supports: The claim that pump-handle removal ended the Broad Street epidemic is a durable heroic myth rather than the evidential core of Snow's work.

sources.title: Causal Inference, Mechanisms, and the Semmelweis Case
supports: Semmelweis combined comparative causal reasoning, quantitative tables, intervention evidence, and animal experiments; later retellings often omit crucial tables and experiments.

sources.title: Shattering the Myth of Semmelweis
supports: The standard portrayal of Semmelweis as an unambiguously excellent reasoner is contested and should not be treated as settled history.

sources.title: Was There a Bacteriological Revolution in Late Nineteenth-Century Medicine?
supports: Bacteriological change was uneven across diseases and practices; a single rapid British revolution remains historically unproven.

sources.title: What Is a Pathogen? Toward a Process View of Host-Parasite Interactions
supports: Pathogenicity depends on host-microbe interactions; pure-culture rules face carriers, unculturable agents, variable hosts, and artificial inoculation limits.

sources.title: A Spirit of Scientific Rigour: Koch's Postulates in Twentieth-Century Medicine
supports: The textbook three-step postulate story simplifies Koch's changing practice, and later medicine repeatedly adapted causal criteria to agents and carrier states.

sources.authors: Samantha Vanderslott; Maile T. Phillips; Virginia E. Pitzer; Claas Kirchhelle
sources.title: Water and Filth: Reevaluating the First Era of Sanitary Typhoid Intervention
supports: Miasmatic and sanitary reformers promoted environmental and sewer interventions whose practical effects cannot be evaluated solely by whether their causal theory was correct.

lineage_nodes.name: Miasmatic and sanitary frameworks
lineage_nodes.surviving_value: They focused attention on filth, crowding, drainage, water, waste, ventilation, and municipal responsibility; several resulting interventions reduced real exposure routes.
lineage_nodes.failed_or_limited_claim: A generic disease-causing foul-air emanation did not identify disease-specific agents or reliably distinguish air, water, contact, vector, and host pathways.

lineage_nodes.name: Snow's cholera transmission account
lineage_nodes.surviving_value: It used household exceptions, spatial patterns, and differing water supplies to support ingestion of contaminated water as cholera's route.
lineage_nodes.failed_or_limited_claim: It did not isolate the causal organism, and pump-handle removal was not the decisive experiment that ended the outbreak.

lineage_nodes.name: Semmelweis's puerperal-fever program
lineage_nodes.component: contact pathway, intervention, and partial material mechanism
lineage_nodes.surviving_value: Comparative mortality, chlorine hand disinfection, and mechanistic experiments supported transmission of harmful material by attendants and a lifesaving control practice.
lineage_nodes.failed_or_limited_claim: Intervention success did not validate every etiological or monocausal statement, and historians disagree about the quality and completeness of his reasoning.

lineage_nodes.name: Pasteur's microbial laboratory program
lineage_nodes.component: microbial ontology, contamination controls, and experimental laboratory method
lineage_nodes.surviving_value: Fermentation and anti-spontaneous-generation work made living microorganisms and controlled contamination experimentally productive explanatory entities.
lineage_nodes.failed_or_limited_claim: These results did not by themselves establish that one particular microorganism caused each particular human disease.

lineage_nodes.name: Koch's disease-specific experimental etiology
lineage_nodes.component: agent-disease linkage through visualization, culture, transmission, and pathology
lineage_nodes.surviving_value: Anthrax and tuberculosis studies joined a specific organism to a specific disease using converging laboratory evidence.
lineage_nodes.failed_or_limited_claim: Pure-culture criteria do not universally fit viruses, unculturable agents, asymptomatic carriers, polymicrobial disease, or variable host responses.

lineage_nodes.name: Host-pathogen-environment process view
lineage_nodes.component: relational pathogenicity and multilevel disease causation
lineage_nodes.surviving_value: It preserves microbes as causal participants while explaining carriers, variable susceptibility, virulence, dose, immunity, co-infection, and environmental exposure.
lineage_nodes.failed_or_limited_claim: A generic process slogan is not enough; each claimed causal contribution still needs disease-specific evidence.

J1_representation_change.reason: A generic atmospheric/environmental cause was replaced for cholera by a specific ingestion and water-supply pathway.

J2_retention_accounting.reason: Environmental clustering and clean-water benefits were retained as phenomena and re-explained through contaminated water, without retaining foul air as the agent.

J3_new_reach.reason: The route explained household exceptions, occupational exposure, and contrasting water-company mortality that generic miasma could not isolate.

J4_complexity_dimensions.reason: The causal route was more specific and conceptually narrower, while exposure tracing and population comparisons increased evidential work.

J5_rival_discrimination.reason: Water-source comparisons and exceptions separated waterborne transmission from local bad-air proximity better than the map alone.

J6_falsifiability_growth.reason: The account risked failure wherever water source and cholera incidence diverged under comparable conditions.

transition_edges.unresolved: The causal agent remained unspecified; route evidence was not yet germ isolation.

transition_edges.claimed_component: puerperal-fever contact pathway and chlorine-hand-disinfection intervention

J1_representation_change.reason: The account localized a transferable harmful material on attendants and instruments rather than a shared ward atmosphere alone.

J2_retention_accounting.reason: Cleaning remained practically valuable, but success was reassigned from odor removal to material-transfer interruption.

J3_new_reach.reason: It connected ward differences, autopsy exposure, individual cases, and prevention through one manipulable pathway.

J4_complexity_dimensions.reason: The intervention rule was simple; the full etiology, disease identity, and alternative causes were not.

J5_rival_discrimination.reason: Mortality changes under disinfection and comparative tables supported a contact contribution, but did not eliminate every rival cause or establish a modern germ ontology.

J6_falsifiability_growth.reason: The account predicted mortality changes with material transfer and disinfection and could fail across clinics, periods, and non-cadaveric cases.

transition_edges.unresolved: The exact agent, multiplicity of causes, and generality beyond the studied setting remained contested.

transition_edges.claimed_component: microbial ontology and controlled laboratory method

J1_representation_change.reason: Living microorganisms and contamination pathways became manipulable experimental entities rather than unspecified poisons or emanations.

J2_retention_accounting.reason: Contagion, contamination, fermentation, and sanitation successes received a common microbial interpretation without preserving all predecessor etiologies.

J3_new_reach.reason: Controlled exposure, sterilization, and organism-specific fermentation generated new questions and laboratory interventions.

J4_complexity_dimensions.reason: A common living-agent ontology compressed several phenomena while demanding new laboratory controls and techniques.

J5_rival_discrimination.reason: Contamination-controlled vessels discriminated spontaneous generation claims, but did not alone distinguish microbes causing particular diseases.

J6_falsifiability_growth.reason: The program exposed claims to controlled-air, contamination, sterilization, and organism-process tests.

transition_edges.unresolved: Human disease-specific etiology required further evidence.

J1_representation_change.reason: The broad possibility of living agents became a disease-specific agent, life cycle, pathology, and transmission claim.

J2_retention_accounting.reason: Earlier route and intervention successes were connected to agent behavior while failed generic etiologies were discarded.

J3_new_reach.reason: The method enabled disease-specific detection, cultivation, experimental reproduction, prevention questions, and differentiation among infections.

J4_complexity_dimensions.reason: Specific etiologies reduced causal ambiguity but increased experimental, technical, and disease-by-disease work.

J5_rival_discrimination.reason: Repeated detection, isolation/culture, inoculation, pathology, and re-identification supplied converging discriminators beyond association alone.

J6_falsifiability_growth.reason: A candidate agent could fail presence, isolation, transmission, pathology, or re-identification tests.

transition_edges.unresolved: The method's domain did not include every pathogen, carrier state, host response, or polymicrobial process.

false_jump_controls.false_claim: Snow ended the Broad Street epidemic by removing the pump handle.
false_jump_controls.reason: The outbreak was already waning; Snow's stronger contribution was the wider comparative route evidence.
He argued for a mode of communication without isolating or identifying the organism.

false_jump_controls.false_claim: Hand disinfection worked, therefore Semmelweis's complete etiology was correct.
false_jump_controls.reason: An action effect supports a pathway contribution but underdetermines the complete mechanism and cause set.

false_jump_controls.false_claim: Sanitation sometimes worked, therefore miasma was approximately the pathogen.
false_jump_controls.reason: An intervention can block a real water/contact/vector route for reasons different from the theory that motivated it.

false_jump_controls.false_claim: Pasteur single-handedly discovered germ theory of human disease.
false_jump_controls.reason: His ontology and experimental controls were crucial nodes, not the entire route-, clinical-, and disease-specific evidential network.

false_jump_controls.false_claim: Finding a microorganism in diseased tissue proves it caused the disease.
false_jump_controls.reason: Specific etiology needs converging evidence about presence, isolation or characterization, transmission/production, pathology, and alternatives.

false_jump_controls.false_claim: Koch's postulates are a universal timeless checklist that every genuine pathogen must satisfy.
false_jump_controls.reason: Carriers, viruses, unculturable agents, host variation, ethics, and polymicrobial disease require type-specific adaptations.

false_jump_controls.false_claim: One germ produces one inevitable disease outcome independently of host and environment.
false_jump_controls.reason: Pathogenicity is often a process involving organism, virulence, dose, host susceptibility/immunity, and environment.

study_2_amendment_tests.finding: Sanitation success can be recovered and re-explained without retaining foul air as the agent.
Snow's route, Semmelweis's intervention, Pasteur's ontology, and Koch's agent-disease method need separate verdicts.
Microbial specificity reduced causal ambiguity while increasing laboratory and disease-by-disease complexity.
Koch-style evidence is powerful within a domain but not universal across carriers, viruses, host variation, or polymicrobial disease.
Effective route/intervention evidence often preceded and underdetermined the agent and complete mechanism.

contract_extension.trigger: The case is a distributed network of complementary component jumps; no single arrow or successful intervention carries the whole explanatory transition.

prior_amendment_status.finding: Sanitation success can be recovered and re-explained without retaining foul air as the agent.

extensions.new_rule: Represent a proposed J-jump as a lineage graph when route, intervention, ontology, method, and mechanism arise in different agents or periods. Credit only the component and evidence actually supplied by each node.
extensions.guardrail: Do not collapse a distributed discovery into a single-hero narrative or transfer later evidence backward to an earlier node.

extensions.new_rule: Record separately: intervention effectiveness, transmission route, causal agent, production mechanism, and full etiology. Success at one level raises but does not automatically satisfy another level's warrant.
extensions.guardrail: An effective action is not by itself proof of the action's proposed mechanism or of a complete cause set.

extensions.new_rule: For causal J-jumps, map which independent evidence modes support the claim: comparative pattern, intervention, localization, visualization, isolation/characterization, reproduction, re-identification, dose/host response, and alternative elimination.
extensions.guardrail: No fixed rung is universal, but an association-only or rhetoric-only candidate cannot be promoted.

extensions.new_rule: State whether the causal claim concerns a necessary agent, sufficient agent, contributing cause, route, virulence factor, susceptible host, or environment. Do not use a generic cause label across these roles.
extensions.guardrail: A microbe's presence and a disease outcome must not be modeled as one inevitable one-to-one relation.

extensions.new_rule: Track conceptual discovery, evidential warrant, community uptake, implementation, and health outcome as separate timelines.
extensions.guardrail: Later acceptance or beneficial policy cannot be back-projected as evidence available to the original proposal, and rejection alone does not prove a proposal was ahead of its time.

contract_extension.revised_j_jump_object: A component-scoped node or linked subgraph with declared lineage, evidence available at the time, retention accounting, causal level, approximation/domain boundary, rivals, and new failure conditions.

results.why_not_sufficient: It handled retention, components, complexity, approximation, and underdetermination, but still modeled a jump too much like one proposal-to-proposal arrow and did not explicitly decouple intervention, route, agent, mechanism, uptake, and outcome.
significant_findings: The miasma-to-germ transition is a network of component jumps, not one Einstein-style moment or one hero's theory.
An effective intervention can precede correct ontology and mechanism; action success and explanatory success must be audited separately.
Wrong theories can motivate beneficial actions when the action intersects the real causal route for a different reason.
Specific microbial causation was a major gain, but microbial presence is not an inevitable disease outcome independently of host and environment.
A credible AI J-jump may be a new synthesis across partially successful nodes rather than a wholly new sentence generated from nothing.

next_case.name: Caloric fluid to kinetic theory of heat
next_case.reason: This tests whether the distributed and intervention-decoupled contract works when an empirically successful conserved-substance model is replaced by a statistical-mechanical representation with different ontology and scale.
next_case.stop_condition: If the contract requires domain-specific exceptions that cannot be expressed through the existing lineage, component, retention, causal-level, and evidence rules, pause historical expansion and reassess whether a general J-jump detector is possible.
